timeline.title: A Short History of Kindness
items: The lady with the lamp
Florence Nightingale nursed soldiers through the night, and changed nursing for ever.
Help for everyone
The Red Cross was founded to care for anyone who was hurt, whichever side they were on.
A day for nurses
International Nurses Day began, held every year on 12 May, Florence Nightingale's birthday.
Every day
Ordinary heroes
Carers, coaches, neighbours and nurses quietly change lives, mostly without anyone saying thank you.
today: Not in the history books yet. But in ours, a real hero.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Kindness
items: No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.
Aesop, The Lion and the Mouse
How far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a weary world.
William Shakespeare, The Merchant of Venice
Kind words can be short and easy to speak, but their echoes are truly endless.
Often credited to Mother Teresa
Gratitude is the memory of the heart.
An old saying
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: thank you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Kindness
items: heart
Good for the heart
Being kind releases oxytocin, a hormone that helps relax blood vessels and calm the heart.
spark
The helper's high
Helping others lights up the brain's reward centres, the same ones that light up for chocolate.
hands
Catching kindness
Studies show that seeing someone be kind makes us more likely to be kind ourselves.
pulse
Thank you matters
Saying thank you makes people more likely to help again. So consider this magazine a very big one.
star
Small things count
People who receive a thank you note often say it meant far more than the sender guessed.
leaf
Kindness lasts
People who do kind things often feel happier for days afterwards.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain how {who} made such a difference to us.

note.title: What we believe a hero is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe the real heroes rarely wear capes. They hold a hand, make the tea, cheer from the side of the pitch and turn up again tomorrow.
{who}, someone wanted to say thank you properly. Not with a card that gets lost, but pages full of you: your words, your kindness, the difference you made.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you changed things for them in a way they will never forget.
